system: mixed legal system based on English common law and Islamic law

constitution.amend: proposed by the monarch; passage requires submission to the Privy Council for Legislative Council review and finalization takes place by proclamation; the monarch can accept or reject changes to the original proposal provided by the Legislative Council
constitution.note: some constitutional provisions suspended since 1962 under a state of emergency, others suspended since independence in 1984

courts.highest: Supreme Court (consists of the Court of Appeal and the High Court, each with a chief justice and 2 judges); Sharia Court (consists the Court of Appeals and the High Court)
courts.judges: Supreme Court judges appointed by the monarch to serve until age 65, and older if approved by the monarch; Sharia Court judges appointed by the monarch for life
courts.lower: Intermediate Court; Magistrates' Courts; Juvenile Court; small claims courts; lower sharia courts
courts.note: Brunei has a dual judicial system of secular and sharia (religious) courts; the Judicial Committee of Privy Council (in London) serves as the final appellate court for civil cases only

citizenship.descent: the father must be a citizen of Brunei

suffrage: 18 years of age for village elections; universal
world: has not submitted an ICJ jurisdiction declaration; non-party state to the ICC
